mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a WPS and a WPQR?
Can Elenchon produce a finalized WPS from captured WPQR data?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Define a preliminary WPS in the app, capture the actual WPQR parameters on the floor, import those real values back beside the procedure, and export a finalized WPS you write from them — with official files uploaded or linked at any stage.

mainEntity.name: How does welder continuity (WPQ) tracking work?

acceptedAnswer.text: A welder's WPQ is held on file, and Elenchon surfaces the qualifying welds behind it from real floor entries — logging 6-month continuity automatically and warning you before a qualification expires, so no welder works outside an approved range.

mainEntity.name: Is welder qualification included in the main platform?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes — the WPS/WPQR/WPQ workflow is a built-in part of Elenchon, not a separate product or paid add-on. Elenchon is one full welding management platform: shop-floor work capture, project structure and BOM import, weld traceability and equipment and consumable control, with qualification managed in the same system rather than bolted on beside it.

Welding qualification software manages the records that prove welds are made by qualified people to qualified procedures — WPS, WPQR and WPQ. Elenchon runs that whole workflow on-premise, so qualification data stays on hardware you own and audit evidence is always a click away.

mainEntity.name: Do you lose anything by keeping qualification records on-premise?

acceptedAnswer.text: No — you gain control without losing reach. Your WPS, WPQR and WPQ records live on an appliance in your facility rather than a shared cloud server, so the evidence auditors care about is under your jurisdiction, not a vendor's. Authorised staff — and even auditors — still reach it from anywhere through Phrakton, our secure network overlay.
